claims.text: The starting material is a CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy without self-lubricating additives.
A self-lubricating secondary phase can be incorporated into the CoCrFeNi matrix with uniform dispersion.
The incorporated secondary phase will remain stable at high temperatures up to 800 °C.
MoS2 is a layered self-lubricating compound suitable as an example of the proposed secondary phase.
Uniformly dispersed secondary-phase particles will form a continuous lubricious tribofilm during sliding.
The tribofilm will alleviate direct metal-to-metal contact.
Alleviating direct metal contact will reduce adhesive wear.
The layered structure of the secondary phase will facilitate easy shear during sliding.
Easy shear and formation of a stable lubricious film will lower the coefficient of friction.
At lower temperatures, the secondary phase will provide immediate lubrication.
At higher temperatures, the tribofilm will resist oxidation-induced degradation and wear.
The modified composite will have a statistically significantly lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi from room temperature to 800 °C.
The modified composite will have a statistically significantly lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi from room temperature to 800 °C.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits particularly high friction and wear near ambient temperature and the high-temperature limit.
Changes in load, sliding speed, vacuum, or humidity may alter tribofilm formation and its effectiveness.
